newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African govt budget funding to peak in August.
newsitem.headline: S.African govt budget funding to peak in August.

text.p: The South African government would spread its funding from the domestic market throughout 1997/98, peaking in August, the finance department said.

In its budget review released with Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's budget speech on Wednesday, the department said funding would continue to take place in the three stocks which were issued in 1996/97 -- the R184, R153 and R157.

A limited amount of R150 stocks would also be made available and zero coupon bonds with maturities later than April 1, 2003 would be made available in those areas where it could be accommodated in terms of the maturity schedule.
In addition, the South African Reserve Bank would make a market in R162, R175 and R177 government stocks.

In terms of the maturity schedule of domestic marketable stock, nominal amounts of about 18 billion rand in R150 stock, 10 billion rand in R184 stock, 52 billion rand in R153 stock and 130 billion rand in R157 stock could still be issued before the upper limit of each stock was reached.

"An amount of five billion rand of R150 stock will be issued during the 1997/98 financial year, while the issue amounts in respect of other funding stocks will be determined by market demand," the review said.
Two billion rand of the borrowing requirement would be financed by an increase in the volume of 91 day and 182 day treasury bills from the current 14.3 billion rand to 16.3 billion rand in issue.
"The government will continue to spread its funding in government stock throughout the financial year," it said.

"Interest payments on government stock of about 7.8 billion rand and redemptions of 8.8 billion rand will result in a funding requirement that will peak during August 1997 and therefore during the first half of the financial year.

"It is not envisaged that these flows will impose undue financing pressure on the markets. The department of finance will make use of an anticipated opening cash balance, deposits by the Corporation for Public Deposits, proceeds from privatisation, prceeds from strategic oil sales and budgeted foreign borrowing to smooth out this cash flow peak."
During his speech, Manuel said that as part of the move to improve the management of government debt, primary dealers in government stock would be appointed.
This called for a closer relationship between the department and the market and a workshop for interested parties was held on February 7.
"A number of issues were identified and several working groups were tasked with doing further work on a number of these issues and report back by the end of March," Manuel said.
On the asset side, the focus had been on cash management and Cabinet had approved the formal establishment of a cash management division in the department.
